functional.text: Send a message one-to-one; it is delivered to every device of the recipient.
Group chats of up to 200 members; a group message reaches every member.
History is kept for 1 year and syncs to any device; offline users catch up on reconnect and get a push notification.
Secondary: online indicator and read receipts.

non_functional.text: Online-to-online delivery latency < 500 ms at p99 (real-time feel).
Messages are never lost once acknowledged to the sender, and appear in the same order on every device.
Highly available: losing a server must only cause a quick reconnect.

assumptions.text: 50M DAU × 40 msgs/day; 20% of DAU connected at peak; peak = 3× average.
~200 B stored per message; media lives in blob storage and is referenced by URL.

out_of_scope.text: End-to-end encryption key management, voice/video calls, media upload pipeline.

api.notes: Catch-up and history paging, used on reconnect and on a new device.

data.name: messages
data.fields: conversation_id (partition key), seq (clustering), message_id, client_msg_id, sender_id, body, created_at
data.why: Append-heavy, read as 'latest N of one conversation': a wide-column store partitioned by conversation fits.

data.name: conversation_members
data.why: Small, relational, read on every group fan-out (cached).

data.name: sessions
data.why: Ephemeral routing state; doubles as presence.

deep_dives.title: Server-to-client transport

options.name: short polling
options.cons: 10M clients × 1 req/s, mostly empty, and up to 1 s delay

options.name: long polling
options.cons: reconnect per message, awkward for sends

options.name: WebSocket
options.pros: one bidirectional connection per device; server pushes instantly
options.cons: stateful servers; need a routing registry

deep_dives.choice: WebSocket, with long polling as a fallback
deep_dives.why: N1 needs the server to speak first; 10M concurrent connections fit on ~150–200 gateways and the statefulness is isolated in that tier.

deep_dives.title: Ordering and duplicates

options.name: per-conversation sequence
options.pros: order where users can see it; scales by conversation
options.cons: one owner per conversation at a time

deep_dives.choice: per-conversation sequence + at-least-once delivery with dedup
deep_dives.why: N2: the chat service assigns seq when it writes (the stream partition keyed by conversation_id is the single owner); retries reuse client_msg_id so the store dedups; clients sort by seq and fetch gaps.

deep_dives.title: Group fan-out

options.name: sender's server delivers to each member synchronously
options.cons: slow ack, one bad gateway stalls the sender

options.name: async fan-out workers off a stream
options.pros: sender acked after one write; workers retry independently

deep_dives.choice: async fan-out workers off a stream
deep_dives.why: With 200-member groups a third of messages fan out ~200×; decoupling keeps sender latency flat and lets delivery retry.

wrapup.bottlenecks: Very active large groups (fan-out cost), the session registry on every delivery (cache locally, shard by user), hot conversation partitions in the message store.
wrapup.failures: Gateway crash: clients reconnect with backoff + jitter to another gateway and sync from last seq. Fan-out worker lag: the stream retains messages and workers replay. Retried sends are deduped by client_msg_id.
wrapup.monitoring: End-to-end delivery latency (send → device ack), connections per gateway, reconnect rate, stream consumer lag, push failure rate.
wrapup.scale: More gateways behind the LB; shard the registry by user; add stream partitions and store nodes; for very large groups switch to pull-on-open instead of per-member fan-out.
wrapup.future: End-to-end encryption, message search, multi-region active-active with per-conversation home regions.
